# CANDIDATE: VOLATILITY_COMPRESSION_BREAKOUT

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

After a period of ATR contraction and narrow range (NR7), a breakout with above-average volume tends to persist, offering a directional edge. This setup captures volatility compression followed by expansion, which often precedes sustained moves as liquidity re-enters the market after a consolidation phase.

## Mechanism

Calculate ATR(14). If ATR today < ATR yesterday < ATR day before (three consecutive contractions) AND today's range (high-low) is the narrowest of the last 7 bars (NR7) AND volume > 1.5 * average volume(20), then enter long if close > high of the NR7 bar, short if close < low of the NR7 bar. Exit shape: Initial stop at opposite side of the NR7 range (long: stop at NR7 low; short: stop at NR7 high). Target at 2x ATR(14) from entry or trail with chandelier exit (ATR*3) after 1R profit. Regime hint: Effective when VIX between 15-25 (moderate) and after 10:30 EST to avoid opening noise; avoid days with major economic releases where volatility expands unpredictably.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account; $1K paper ~= 14% headline P&L scaling due to 50% per-trade risk cap and minimum 3-contract structure.
2. **Sample bias:** Proposed strategy would require backtesting on 16-month SPY 5m data (Jan 2025-Jun 2026). Risk of overfit exists due to multiple parameter combinations (ATR period, NR lookback, volume multiplier, VIX filters) without out-of-sample validation.
3. **Out-of-sample:** NEEDS-OOS (no walk-forward held-out window performed yet).
4. **Real-fills:** NEEDS-REAL-FILLS (no validation against real OPRA spreads/slippage on top 3 J days).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day: whipsaw in low-VIX trending markets (e.g., Nov-Dec 2025) causing repeated stops; max drawdown scenario: consecutive losses during volatility expansion days where NR7 breakouts fail; blow-up scenario: volatility expansion day with gap-through NRW stop (e.g., FOMC surprise) causing catastrophic loss beyond NRW stop due to slippage.
6. **Concentration:** unknown -- requires Stage-1 backtest to determine if top-5 days drive X% of P&L.
